words.meaning: Work out a numerical answer. Show your working.
words.example: Calculate the area of the rectangle.

words.meaning: Give a sensible approximate answer, usually by rounding first.
Write every step so the examiner can follow your method.
Give a short answer in words or numbers.
Fill in the missing parts of a table, diagram, sentence or sequence.
Say what is the same and what is different, using comparative words (more, less, faster…).
Say what something is like or what happens. For data, give the pattern using both variables.
words.example: Describe the pattern in the results.

words.meaning: Give reasons. Use “because” or “so” to link cause and effect.
Pick out or name something from information given.
Give a short, factual answer. No explanation needed.
Say what you think will happen, ideally with a reason based on evidence or science.
Apply what you know to a new situation. There may be more than one acceptable answer.
words.example: Suggest how to improve the investigation.

words.meaning: Put items into groups or into the correct sequence.
words.example: Order these fractions from smallest to largest.

words.meaning: Give a number to a stated degree of accuracy (nearest 10, one decimal place…).
